editorial:
Imagine being a super strict music teacher who thinks anything other than classical music is noise. That is exactly who you meet in this fun flick. Don is a total stiff who lives in a boring town where everyone follows the rules. He heads to New York City to sell some of his music, but he ends up staying with his wild aunt. She is the complete opposite of him and hangs out with the swing music crowd. The whole vibe shifts when Don accidentally drinks a strong cocktail thinking it is just lemonade, which finally lets him loosen up and embrace the beat.

Dick Powell does a great job showing the change from a grumpy professor to a guy who actually knows how to have a good time. The music numbers are catchy, and the pacing keeps you smiling throughout. While some of the jokes feel a bit old, the charm makes up for it. You should definitely check this out if you like old-school comedies with a heart.
endingExplained: After spending time in the city, Don realizes that swing music is just as valuable as the classical stuff he taught. He stops being so stiff and finds a middle ground between the two styles. He eventually finds love and success by blending his skills. The movie wraps up with him happily accepting the modern music world, proving that it is never too late to change your mind and start having fun.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage movies and catchy tunes.
